entries.content:
# Source: gdu (dundee/gdu), pointers for integrators

Clone: research/sources/dundee-gdu @ 848a5dd (2026-09-21), MIT, 5,999 stars, Go 1.26. Report: research/reports/sources/dundee-gdu.md. Task T-0032.

## Take / port
- **Dataless opt-out (macOS)**: pkg/fs/dataless_darwin.go:53-77, `setiopolicy_np(IOPOL_TYPE_VFS_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES=3, IOPOL_SCOPE_PROCESS=0, IOPOL_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES_OFF=1)`. It is called once before the scan (cmd/gdu/app/app.go:781-786). Reading a dataless file afterwards fails with EDEADLK, so the viewer and preview must handle that.
- **Treemap node budget**: webui/tree.go:299-363. A max-heap by usage expands best-first up to maxTreeNodes = 5000, so the map fills the largest areas first. The layout is d3 squarify (webui/frontend/src/components/treemap/treemap.ts:22-46) with a minArea cull (treeLayout.ts).
- **Relocation check idea**: webui/tree.go:209-265 `checkNotRelocated` re-resolves the parent chain before RemoveAll. It is string-based and has a TOCTOU window, which its own comment admits ("needs openat-style traversal"). Do it fd-relative.
- **Local web action guard**: webui/server.go:80-150 (loopback, same-origin, per-run token, DNS-rebinding host check).
- **Accounting discipline**: pkg/analyze/file.go:176-216 has one `resolveDirStats` plus `EmptyDirSize = 512`, locked by `TestEmptyDirStatsAcrossAnalyzers` (analyzer_parity_test.go). docs/adr/0001 makes the displayed item count authoritative. CONTEXT.md is a useful glossary (stopped vs abandoned scan, bar denominator).
- **Safe user-command pattern**: pkg/remove/trash_command.go:60-110 runs `sh -c <script> gdu <absPath>`. The path goes in as $1 and is never interpolated.

## Do not port
- pkg/analyze/wait.go: a custom WaitGroup whose Add does not re-arm after the count hits 0. Verified by TestProbeWaitGroupRearm. It is the root cause of F-0007 (TopDirAnalyzer, `gdu -n`).
- The engine is path-string based: os.ReadDir + lstat per file (parallel.go:81,115), so PATH_MAX subtrees are dropped (F-0008). There is one goroutine per pending dir plus a collector goroutine per dir (parallel.go:108,196-205). The semaphore is a package global sized at init, so `--max-cores` does not resize it (parallel.go:13 vs app.go:436-445).
- Hard links: inode only, without dev (dir_unix.go:28-30). The first link reached gets the bytes, in goroutine completion order (gdu #439, class F-0054). Delete subtracts raw sizes (F-0063).
- Deletion: remove.go:11-19 `os.RemoveAll(item.GetPath())`, with no identity check. Trash is refused on macOS (trash_darwin.go:11-14), which is honest but gives no undo.

## Gotchas found (findings)
- F-0061: `-f` import keeps delete on and trusts names. An absolute or `../` name deletes outside the root (import.go:134-140 + file.go:463-466). ncdu disables delete on import (ncdu.1:79-84).
- F-0062: a `--type` filter plus `d` deletes the whole folder. The TUI checks only time filters (tui.go:722-763); the web UI checks all filters (webui/handlers.go:127).
- F-0063: a hard-link delete makes a folder negative (-4 MiB) and drops the total 4 MiB below disk.

## Probe harness (reusable for any Go source)
research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh: `go test -vet=off -overlay <json>`. The overlay replaces heavy files (badger storage.go and the modernc sqlite driver) with stubs, masks the package's own *_test.go with "", and injects probe tests into an *existing* package dir. The clone stays untouched, the build takes ~7 s, and there is no modernc compile. Two gotchas: vet and the test binary chdir into the package dir, so a brand-new overlay-only directory fails ("chdir ... no such file"). Use an existing package (external `_test` package) or pass -vet=off.

## Numbers (this Mac, 311k-entry fixture)
- Full tree (`gdu-go -p -o /dev/null`): 1.9-2.0 s, peak footprint 181 / 187 MB. That includes the export's whole-JSON bytes.Buffer (report/export.go:245-270), so ~600 B/entry is an upper bound.
- `-n` top-dir: 1.2 s, 25 MB footprint. Totals were 2,340,888,576 vs 2,359,623,680 across 2 runs, which is F-0007 again.

entries.name: Source: MacTools (DiskClean plugin)
entries.content:
Source: ggbond268/MacTools (GPL-3.0-only at HEAD bf6550a, 1,218 stars). Report: research/reports/sources/ggbond268-mactools.md. Task T-0033. Findings F-0064, F-0065. Clone: research/sources/ggbond268-mactools (gitignored). Probes: research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/ (they copy GPL files from the clone at run time).

LICENSE TRAP / OPPORTUNITY
- The repo was Apache-2.0 from a8627a0 (2026-05-16) until bcd9f9f (2026-08-27, "migrate to GPL-3.0-only"). LICENSING.md says pre-transition grants are not revoked.
- The last Apache revision is 9197035650b67f1c313960e8b1dded7a710264dd. There the whole DiskClean 2.0 engine (df1dcdd by rkrkrkk, 2026-07-30) is byte-identical to HEAD: WorkerPool, FastWalker, SlowWalker, DirectoryTreeWalker, RootOpener, RemovalPrimitive, StagingJournal, StagingReconciler, SafetyPolicy, SizeCache, Plan, PurgeScanner, InstallerScanner, RunningAppLock and 11 more. The Executor differs by 67 diff lines.
- To reuse: fetch with `gh api "repos/ggbond268/MacTools/contents/<path>?ref=9197035650b67f1c313960e8b1dded7a710264dd"`, keep the Apache notice and credit "MacTools contributors" in NOTICE. NEVER copy from HEAD.
- GPL-only, ideas only: StorageExplorer (added 2026-09-06), Sources/MacToolsFileSystem (2026-09-07). The Apache-era full parser is in Plugins/DiskClean/Sources/DiskCleanBulkAttributeParser.swift@9197035.

KEY FILES (Plugins/DiskClean/Sources/)
- DiskCleanWorkerPool.swift: DiskCleanResumeGate (:5-49) uses claim() then deliver(), so bookkeeping lands before the resume. Resident Threads with 1 MiB stacks, abandon plus device blacklist plus circuit break after 3 (:265-321). The timeout fires at the SAME deadline the walker checks. The walker won 10/10 in the probe, but a lost race blacklists the whole volume for the life of the process. Replace the wall clock with a progress-heartbeat watchdog.
- DiskCleanDirectoryTreeWalker.swift: a single-thread explicit-stack DFS with an fd-anchored openat(O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK). It drains child directories before reading the next batch, so fds are bounded by depth. The devid guard runs on EVERY entry (:168-172), which is the correct way to catch mount points, because bulk devid does not flag the mount point itself.
- DiskCleanSizingModels.swift: typed completeness, `.complete` or `.partial{timedOut, permissionDenied, unsupportedVolume, crossedMountPoint, walkError}`. DiskCleanModels.swift:324-327: only complete results are cleanable (F-0065 is about this coupling).
- DiskCleanRootOpener.swift: O_NOFOLLOW_ANY|O_NONBLOCK, MNT_LOCAL, ELOOP disambiguated through a parent fd plus fstatat. Callers must pass physical paths: /var and /tmp fail with ELOOP. The probe hit this, so pwd -P the temp dirs.
- DiskCleanRemovalPrimitive.swift: verify identity, journal begin + fsync, renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL) to ".mactools-staged-<UUID>", re-verify, then trash or prewalk + irreversible delete, with rollback via RENAME_EXCL. GOTCHA (F-0064): the staged name reaches the Trash hidden, and Put Back restores the hidden name.
- DiskCleanPlan.swift: DiskCleanValidatedPlan has a fileprivate init that only DiskCleanPlanner.makePlan can call (the mint pattern). ancestorViolation guards exclusions and reserved roots. Expiry gate 300 s (DiskCleanModels.swift:358-365), confirmation window min(60 s, remaining).
- DiskCleanScanEngine.swift:864-960: CandidateAssembler, which does ancestor decomposition when globs nest. Ownership goes to the longest fixed glob prefix, and aliases are merged.
- DiskCleanRuleCatalogV2.swift: 54 targets, 40 low and 16 medium. Rules live in Swift, not in a data file. `~/Library/Caches/*` is low risk and pre-selected, with NO running-app lock (F-0015 class). `cache.macos-app-state` includes `~/Library/Autosave Information/*` under the consequence "windows may not restore" (F-0027 class).
- DiskCleanFullDiskAccess.swift: opens the USER TCC.db, then Safari/Bookmarks.plist. Both are really FDA-protected, so this does not repeat F-0001.
- getattrlistbulk parser: never request ATTR_CMN_ERROR (it keeps 4 bytes even when its returned bit is 0). Check that the end of the fixed section equals ATTR_CMN_NAME.attr_dataoffset. 0 mismatches on APFS (parser_layout_probe.sh).

STORAGEEXPLORER (GPL, ideas only)
- The scanner is DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform with 4-6 workers, a 30 s directory-listing cache invalidated by FSEvents, and packages treated as atomic. SF_DATALESS directories are not descended.
- Deterministic hard-link charging: the lexicographically smallest path gets the bytes (StorageExplorerScanner.swift:295-311, 421-462). This fixes F-0054.
- BUG: the mount guard compares bulk devid for directories only (:282, 312-316). ATTR_CMN_DEVID of a mount-point entry is the COVERED device (verified in /System/Volumes: VM, Preboot, Update, xarts, Hardware, iSCPreboot). It counted +64 MiB from a mounted image's root files. Use ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS (F-0031).
- Trash stages to <parent>/.mactools-trash-<UUID>/<name>, so the Trash entry keeps the visible name, then rmdirs the staging folder. Put Back target: unverified.
- Treemap: binary-split layout (not squarified), 48/18/10 children per level plus "Other", max 500 rects. Keeps only the top 10k files (the docs say 50k).

NUMBERS
- FastWalker, single thread: 34-40k files/s on a 728k-file tree larger than the vnode cache, 160-190k files/s warm. The per-item cap is 20 s, the global cap 300 s, with 3 items at a time.

entries.name: Source: homebrew-cask zap stanzas (formulae.brew.sh cask.json)
entries.content:
Durable pointers for whoever integrates the Homebrew cask uninstall data into macontrol (T-0035, 2026-09-23). Full report: research/reports/sources/homebrew-homebrew-cask.md. Findings: F-0066, F-0067, F-0068.

## Where things are
- **Feed:** https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask.json. Unsigned, 18.9 MB, 7,755 casks, regenerated minutes after merges. Local copy at research/sources/homebrew-homebrew-cask/cask.json (Last-Modified 2026-09-23 07:42:02 GMT).
  - Signed twin: `api/cask.jws.json`, PS512 JWS, kid `homebrew-1`. The key is `Library/Homebrew/api/homebrew-1.pem` and the verifier is `Library/Homebrew/api.rb:338-379`.
- **Sources:** research/sources/homebrew-homebrew-cask/repo, a sparse depth-1 clone of Homebrew/homebrew-cask@0e47c3a with all `Casks/**/*.rb`. Use the `.rb` files when you need the `#{version...}` templates, which the feed has already resolved.
- **Engine** (Homebrew/brew@570982948a, local /opt/homebrew):
  - `Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb`: order `:23-35`, launchctl `:216-277`, wildcard `:173-181`, pkgutil `:592-600`, delete `:603-616`, trash `:619-643`, rmdir `:651-700`, guards `:139-170`.
  - `cask/pkg.rb`: receipt removal.
  - `cask/macos.rb:6-379`: SYSTEM_DIRS + UNDELETABLE_PATHS seed list.
  - `cask/utils.rb:95-133`: permission fallback. Do not copy.
  - `dev-cmd/generate-zap.rb`: disk scanner and normalizers.
  - `cask/ci/zap_check.rb`: CI oracle pattern.
  - `rubocops/cask/uninstall_wildcard.rb`: a wildcard needs at least 3 ID parts.
- **Scripts** (macontrol-owned):
  - `research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/analyze_zap.py` writes `zap_stats.json` (all counts).
  - `matcher_coverage.py` writes `matcher_coverage.txt` (which key finds which share of the paths).
  - `wildcard_probe.rb` runs brew's resolver on fake input.

## Feed format gotchas
- `artifacts` is a list of one-key dicts: `{"zap":[{"trash":[...],"rmdir":[...]}]}`. Values are a string OR an array; flatten them.
- `variations` holds per-OS/arch overrides of `artifacts` (114 casks have a zap that differs). Tags include `x86_64_linux`: drop them.
- Placeholders to substitute: `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX` (19 paths), `$APPDIR` (16), `/$HOME` (0 in zap today). `~` is literal: expand it to the user's home.
- There is no bundle-ID field. Take the bundle ID from `uninstall.quit` / `signal`, or from `Saved Application State/<id>.savedState` in the zap (2,791 of 4,716 zap casks yield one).
- Globs are Ruby `Pathname.glob`: case-insensitive on APFS (verified), `*` does not match a leading dot, braces work, and `[0-9]` (12 uses) and `**` (3) occur.
- `#{version.major}` / `major_minor` interpolation is frozen in the feed (179 casks, 630 lines). Rebuild templates from the `.rb` (F-0068).
- The `@variant` suffix (`firefox@beta`) is the same product. Merge on the base token for ownership counts.

## Semantics to keep
- Order: early_script, launchctl, quit, signal, login_item, kext, script, pkgutil, delete, trash, rmdir.
- `rmdir` means remove if empty, recursively, ignoring `.DS_Store` and never following a symlink. Use it for vendor folders.
- zap is documented to remove "shared resources" and says "other applications may be affected" (docs/Cask-Cookbook.md:1357-1364). NEVER treat zap paths as preselectable-exact. Classify them into own / shared / user-content first (F-0066; this overrides the "cask zap path = exact" tier in F-0011's after).
- launchctl entries assume plist file name == label and that the label is current. Both can be stale (F-0055). Resolve jobs from on-disk plists + `launchctl print gui/<uid>|system`, anchored and in any state (F-0067).
- pkgutil: `pkgutil --pkgs=REGEX` is anchored (verified). brew removes every BOM file with no reference count; munki's rmpkgs.swift:373-390 is the model.

## Numbers worth remembering
- **Size:** 4,716 zap casks; 21,517 zap path entries (base); 2,187 globbed.
- **Shipping:** a zap+uninstall+app subset is 2.15 MB, 313 KB gzipped.
- **Matcher ceiling on curated paths:** bundle ID 64.8%, +app name 87.5%, +vendor prefix 93.5%. The last 6.5% are Team-ID group containers, vendor folders and user content.
- **Risky paths:** 272 zap paths in user-content roots; 290 literal paths shared by 2+ products; 78 uninstall pkgutil/launchctl IDs shared by 2+ products (Office licensing).

## License
BSD-2-Clause, "Copyright © 2013, Paul Hinze & Contributors". Reproduce the notice, conditions and disclaimer in the app's Acknowledgements. Code and data may be copied.

## Tooling gotcha
`brew ruby <script>` switches Homebrew developer mode ON as a side effect. Run `brew developer off` afterwards.

entries.name: Source: munki removepackages / rmpkgs
entries.content:
Durable pointers for whoever builds macontrol's "remove a pkg-installed app / remove by receipt" feature. Source: munki/munki@28d92fe (Apache-2.0; `rmpkgs.swift` has the same blob in v7.3.0 and v7.4.0b1). Report: research/reports/sources/munki-munki.md. Task T-0037. Findings F-0069, F-0071.

## Key files and functions (paths relative to research/sources/munki-munki)
- `code/cli/munki/shared/installer/rmpkgs.swift` (670 lines) is the whole engine.
  - `getPkgMetaData` :206-233 normalises `install-location`: strips `./` and a trailing `/`. The forms `""`, `"/"` and relative `"Applications"` all occur on this Mac (Karabiner, macFUSE, Cloudflare WARP).
  - `getBomFilesForPkg` :236-254 runs `lsbom -s /private/var/db/receipts/<id>.bom`. `getFilesForPkg` :257-273 skips lsbom for `com.apple.*` and falls back to `pkgutil --files` with a 10 s timeout.
  - `importFromPkgutil` :284-324 runs one `pkgutil --regexp --pkg-info-plist '.*'` and splits the concatenated plists.
  - `getPathsToRemove` :373-389 is THE idea to keep: paths(selected) minus paths(all other receipts).
  - `removeFilesystemItems` :514-594 deletes bottom-up (sorted, reversed). Directories go only if empty or holding only `.DS_Store`. It checks the type with lstat (`utils/fileutils.swift:28-34`).
  - `forgetPkgFromAppleDB` :411-420 runs `pkgutil --forget`.
- Package-level reference counting (a receipt shared by 2 catalog items is never removed): `code/cli/munki/shared/updatecheck/analyze.swift:1021-1062`.
- Python predecessor (the better reference for edge cases): `code/client/munkilib/installer/rmpkgs.py`. It has bound-parameter id lookup and all-or-nothing validation (:471-510), a 4-source staleness check (:62-103) and non-recursive `os.rmdir` (:719-736).

## Gotchas
- Do NOT port `pathIsBundle` (:466-497). It compares the undotted `pathExtension` with a dotted list, so it is always false (F-0069). `URLResourceValues.isPackage` is true for .app and .plugin and FALSE for .framework (verified), so keep an undotted extension list as well.
- Do NOT port `quoteAndJoin` (:354-357). Double-quoted ids are identifiers in SQLite, so `"pkgid"` selects every receipt (F-0071). Use an in-memory `[pkgid: Receipt]` and `Set<String>`. No SQLite is needed.
- Forget receipts only after every planned path is gone. munki forgets them unconditionally and returns 0 (:654-669).
- BOMs hold mode, size and CRC32: `lsbom -p fmsc <bom>` gives, for example, `./Applications/Karabiner-Elements.app/Contents/Info.plist	100644	1649	3735891025`. Use them for an identity check before deleting. munki throws them away (`lsbom -s`).
- BOM locations: `/private/var/db/receipts/<id>.bom` (third-party receipts plus `com.apple.pkg.Xcode`) and `/Library/Apple/System/Library/Receipts/<id>.bom` (other Apple receipts, 25 here). munki only looks in the first.
- Speed: `lsbom -s` on the Xcode BOM took 0.12 s against 1.59 s for `pkgutil --files` (157k lines). munki's full DB rebuild over 32 receipts and 276k paths took 4.4 s.
- Nothing boots out a LaunchDaemon or LaunchAgent before its plist is deleted (the class of F-0023). Deletes are permanent `FileManager.removeItem` as root (the class of F-0012).
- GarageBand/Logic: the munki wiki says the old MAContent10 CoreContent2 and v3 packs share ONE package id (GarageBand.md:46). Since Jan 2026, Logic/MainStage content ships as .aar archives with no pkg receipt (GarageBand.md:4-5). Receipts will not cover all loop content (unverified here: no content is installed on this Mac).

## Probe
- `research/bench/munki-munki/run.sh fixture|rebuild` compiles munki's own files unmodified, with `stubs.swift` stubbing only logging and prefs. `fixture` is safe (all paths in `mktemp -d`, `noUpdateApplePkgDB: true`). `rebuild` is read-only against the real receipts. Output: `results-2026-09-23.txt`. Reuse `main.swift`'s fixture (a bundle with an extra updater file and a user plugin, plus a dylib shared by 2 receipts) as macontrol's acceptance test.

entries.name: Source: Homebrew brew (cask uninstall artifact)
entries.content:
Source journal: Homebrew/brew cask uninstall engine. Task T-0036, report `research/reports/sources/homebrew-brew.md`. The data side (cask.json stanzas) is T-0035 / `homebrew-homebrew-cask.md`.

## Pinned versions
- Read at Homebrew/brew@3f12c3e (2026-09-22). Sparse clone: `research/sources/homebrew-brew` (cone: cask, test/cask, test/support, utils, extend, os, services).
- The installed `/opt/homebrew@570982948a` (7.0.6) has byte-identical `abstract_uninstall.rb`, `cask/utils.rb`, `extend/os/mac/cask/utils/trash.rb` and `cask/pkg.rb`.
- License: BSD-2-Clause. We may copy code or data with the notice kept. Needs a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry if the guard lists are copied.

## Key files and functions (paths under Library/Homebrew/)
- `cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb`
  - `ORDERED_DIRECTIVES` :23-35 is the order to port. The reasons are in the comments at :82, :214, :439, :517 and :555.
  - Dispatch is at :186-199.
  - `each_resolved_path` :139-170 does ~ expansion, rejects relative paths and `.`/`..`, globs, filters with `undeletable?`, and turns EPERM into the FDA hint.
  - `find_launchctl_with_wildcard` :172-181 has a bug (F-0067). `uninstall_launchctl` :214-277 uses `launchctl remove`, not bootout.
  - `uninstall_quit` :91-128 uses JXA with a 10 s timeout. `hosting_brew?` / `ancestor_bundle_ids` :367-400.
  - `expand_bundle_id` + `wildcard_pattern` :343-365 give the anchored, case-insensitive wildcard (the correct version).
  - `uninstall_signal` :443-478, `uninstall_login_item` :488-515 (System Events, legacy only), `uninstall_kext` :518-553.
  - `uninstall_pkgutil` :592-600, `uninstall_delete` :603-616 (always sudo rm -rf), `uninstall_trash` / `trash_paths` :619-643.
  - `recursive_rmdir` / `uninstall_rmdir` :650-700 (.DS_Store counts as empty, symlinks are not followed).
- `cask/artifact/uninstall.rb:20-54`: on upgrade/reinstall, skips :signal and :quit (when asked), and runs :rmdir in the post phase. `cask/artifact/zap.rb:11-13` runs everything.
- `cask/installer.rb:763-777`: `zap` = `uninstall_artifacts`, then the zap stanzas, then purge the Caskroom.
- `cask/artifact/abstract_artifact.rb:72-127`: the cross-artifact `sort_order` (Uninstall first, Zap last).
- `cask/macos.rb`: `SYSTEM_DIRS` :6-236 (227 entries), `UNDELETABLE_PATHS` :241-378 (133 ~ entries + SYSTEM_DIRS), exact-match `undeletable?` :387-389. The TODO at :239 admits there is no subtree protection.
- `cask/pkg.rb`: `Pkg#uninstall` :29-60 does BOM files → specials → dirs deepest-first via `cask/utils/rmdir.sh` → root → `pkgutil --forget`. It never checks other owners.
- `extend/os/mac/cask/utils/trash.rb:16-38` calls `trashItemAtURL` through `os/mac/ffi/foundation.rb:12-67`. On failure it runs `gain_permissions`, which changes metadata (F-0070).
- `cask/utils.rb:95-153`: `gain_permissions` (chflags 000, chmod u+rwx, chmod -N, sudo chown -R) and `ownership_problem?`.
- `os/mac/ffi/libproc.rb:35-46`: parent PID via `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO)`, which works through root-owned ancestors. `os/mac/ffi/app_kit.rb:22-39`: bundle ID for a PID.
- `services/system.rb:131-148`: `launchctl_find_service` (print in gui/user domains, then list).
- Lint-only protections: `rubocops/cask/uninstall_wildcard.rb` (at least 3 ID parts) and `rubocops/cask/shared_filelist_glob.rb`. No cop covers broad trash or delete paths.

## Probes (reuse them)
- `research/bench/homebrew-brew/wildcard_probe.rb <pattern>...`: the real `find_launchctl_with_wildcard` against live `launchctl list`. Read-only.
- `research/bench/homebrew-brew/trash_fallback_probe.rb <scratchdir>`: Case A (real commands, fixture only) and Case B (recorded commands, never runs sudo).
- `research/bench/homebrew-brew/pkg_shared_probe.rb <pkgid> [regex]`: the real `pkgutil_bom_files`, read-only. It never calls `#uninstall`.
- Run with `HOMEBREW_DEVELOPER=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew ruby <probe>`. Without `HOMEBREW_DEVELOPER=1`, `brew ruby` permanently turns developer mode on. Undo that with `brew developer off`.

## Gotchas for the integrator
- Port the ORDER, not the mechanisms:
  - replace `launchctl remove` with `bootout`, found from plist `Label`/`Program` (F-0023, F-0055, F-0067)
  - replace JXA quit with `NSRunningApplication.terminate` (Automation-grant behaviour unverified)
  - replace System Events login items with a BTM/SMAppService listing
- Never port `gain_permissions`. Route root-owned items to the helper and keep their metadata (F-0070).
- The pkg receipt removal needs a per-file owner check (`pkgutil --file-info`, or munki's reference count; F-0066 "after").
- The guard lists are a good seed, but the check must be subtree-aware and use canonical identity (F-0024, F-0039).
- brew has no dry run. macontrol's preview must list every resolved path (after glob) before anything runs.
- Unverified:
  - whether launchd execs a non-root-owned Program (decides how severe F-0070 is)
  - whether `NSRunningApplication.terminate()` needs an Automation grant
  - whether the `File.readable?(TCC dir)` FDA probe gives false positives

entries.name: Source: KnockKnock
entries.content:
Source: KnockKnock (objective-see/KnockKnock@914f2c0, GPL-3.0, study only). Clone: research/sources/objective-see-knockknock. Report: research/reports/sources/objective-see-knockknock.md. Task T-0038. Findings F-0072, F-0073.

## What it is
A persistence enumerator (20 plugins) with no deletion (AppDelegate.m:17 TODO). Use it as the catalogue of where apps leave background items, not as code to port.

## Location catalogue (the facts to re-express as macontrol data; ~ = every user when root)
- launchd plists: /System/Library/LaunchDaemons, /Library/LaunchDaemons, /System/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchAgents (ItemEnumerator.m:21). MISSING and needed: <app>/Contents/Library/LaunchAgents|LaunchDaemons (SMAppService, key BundleProgram), /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools (#15).
- launchd enable/disable overrides: /private/var/db/com.apple.xpc.launchd/disabled.plist (system) and disabled.<uid>.plist (per user), both 0644 (utilities.m:756-862, domain logic LaunchItems.m:303-423).
- BTM db (macOS 13+): /private/var/db/com.apple.backgroundtaskmanagement/BackgroundItems-v<N>.btm, 0644 root, needs FDA (read as uid 501 on 26.6). NSKeyedArchiver root key "store" -> Storage.itemsByUserIdentifier{userUUID: [ItemRecord]} + mdmPayloadsByIdentifier.
  ItemRecord fields: uuid, name, developerName, teamIdentifier, type, disposition, identifier, url, executablePath, generation, bundleIdentifier, associatedBundleIdentifiers, container (parent identifier), embeddedItems, bookmark, lightweightRequirement (DumpBTM dumpBT_Internal.h:36-56).
  type bits: 0x2 app, 0x4 login item, 0x8 agent, 0x10 daemon, 0x20 developer, 0x10000 legacy, 0x80000 curated (dumpBTM.m:380-431). Seen on 26.6 and unknown to DumpBTM: 0x40 mdimporter, 0x80 docktile, 0x800 appex.
  disposition bits: 0x1 enabled, 0x2 allowed, 0x4 hidden, 0x8 notified (dumpBTM.m:469-520).
  GOTCHA: an SMAppService agent's executablePath is bundle-relative ("Contents/...") and its url.path is "/Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/x.plist". Join both to the parent record's url (container == parent.identifier). KnockKnock does not, so the item disappears (F-0072, #49, #50).
- Legacy login items: LSSharedFileList kLSSharedFileListSessionLoginItems (LoginItems.m:96-200); pre-13 per-user ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.backgroundtaskmanagementagent/backgrounditems.btm (bookmarks in $objects, LoginItems.m:301-391); <=10.12 ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginitems.plist (alias records).
- App-embedded login items: <app>/Contents/Library/LoginItems/*.app (LoginItems.m:506-580).
- System extensions: /Library/SystemExtensions/db.plist -> extensions[] {state == "activated_enabled", originPath} (SystemExtensions.m:49-85). The staged copy lives under /Library/SystemExtensions/<uuid>/ (unverified layout).
- Kexts: /System/Library/Extensions, /Library/Extensions (Kexts.m:20). Not covered: /Library/StagedExtensions, kexts inside bundles.
- App extensions: `pluginkit -vmA` ('+' = user-enabled; space = no election; path starts at the first '/') (Extensions.m:60-190); Finder Sync list: ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.preferences.extensions.FinderSync.plist key displayOrder, each checked via `pluginkit -mi <id> -v` (Extensions.h:15, Extensions.m:94-120).
- QuickLook generators, Spotlight importers (/System/Library/Spotlight, /Library/Spotlight, ~/Library/Spotlight), Dock tile plugins (Info.plist NSDockTilePlugIn), authorization plugins (/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins), Directory Services plugins (/Library/DirectoryServices/PlugIns), cron (/private/var/at/tabs), periodic (/etc/periodic/*), emond (/etc/emond.d), login/logout hooks (com.apple.loginwindow.plist), shell configs, browser extensions (Safari/Chrome/Firefox/Opera profile paths in BrowserExtensions.m:24-47).

## Semantics worth copying (as behaviour, clean-room)
- Auto-run = RunAtLoad | KeepAlive (bool or dict) | StartOnMount | any of StartInterval, StartCalendarInterval, WatchPaths, QueueDirectories, LaunchEvents, Sockets, MachServices | legacy OnDemand=false when RunAtLoad/KeepAlive are absent. A plist 'Disabled' key loses to a launchctl-enable override (LaunchItems.m:429-546).
- Global agents load into every user's gui domain: enabled if explicitly enabled in any domain, disabled only if disabled in all (LaunchItems.m:303-423).
- Plist keys are case-insensitive in practice, so lower-case them before lookup (LaunchItems.m:100-108). A relative Program resolves via the job's EnvironmentVariables.PATH, not ours (:200-259).
- An Apple-signed binary started by a non-/System plist is NOT an Apple item (BTM.m:161-170, LaunchItems.m:182-190). Use this in macontrol's protected-item guard.
- Open untrusted files with O_NONBLOCK and check by fstat (regular file, size cap) so FIFOs and devices cannot hang the scan (utilities.m:520-565).
- Resolve login-item bookmarks with no UI and no mounting (LoginItems.m:163-164, 247-248).

## Gotchas / do not port
- File.initWithParams returns nil for a missing path (Results/File.m:59-75). Every plugin then drops the item. Commit e38cad0 (2026-09-11) removed the "(file not found)" fallback on purpose. macontrol needs the opposite: surface these items as `orphaned`.
- BTM decoding dlopens the daemon binary backgroundtaskmanagementd for its private classes (dumpBTM.m:30-35). It works on 26.6 but is GPL, private and fragile. Use it only as a test oracle: research/bench/objective-see-knockknock/run.sh btm.
- DumpBTM getPath takes lastObject of an unsorted listing (dumpBTM.m:364-368). Pick the highest -vN yourself.
- hasFDA() probes the system TCC.db first (utilities.m:1737): the class of F-0001, a false "granted".
- Whole-app root relaunch via AppleScript (utilities.m:2057-2140): F-0073. Use an SMAppService daemon plus setCodeSigningRequirement (macOS 13+, verified in the SDK header NSXPCConnection.h:118).
- The app inventory uses system_profiler SPApplicationsDataType (2.8 s, 374 apps here). A failure stalls DockTiles for 5 min (DockTiles.m:66-83).
- There are no tests. There is a binary blob with no build step (Libraries/BTM/libDumpBTM.a, arm64+x86_64, 13.3 SDK).

## Probes (research/bench/objective-see-knockknock/)
- run.sh btm: 42 records on this Mac: 5 parents, 11 without an exe (appex/mdimporter/docktile/developer), 13 disabled, 15 shown, 1 loaded agent dropped.
- run.sh launchd: missing-program plists in the scanned folders: 0 here.
- run.sh sp: times system_profiler.

entries.name: User direction: UI familiar to PureMac + Radix
entries.content:
## USER DIRECTION (2026-09-23, overrides any conflicting UI choice): make the UI familiar to PureMac and Radix

The user loves the UI/UX of both PureMac and Radix and wants macontrol to feel close to them, not a new visual language. Both are MIT licensed, so their UI code may be adapted (keep the MIT notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the About screen). Clones: `research/sources/momenbasel-puremac`, `research/sources/colinvkim-radix`. Reports: `research/reports/sources/momenbasel-puremac.md`, `colinvkim-radix.md` (UI sections).

**Cleanup side (Overview, Clean, Uninstall) looks and feels like PureMac:**
- `NavigationSplitView` sidebar app, dashboard with a health ring + storage donut + Swift Charts category bars (`DashboardCharts.swift`), cleanup review with search/size/age/sort filters and the "selected rows hidden by filter" warning, app list for uninstall.
- Keep the delight touches (confetti on clean, respects Reduce Motion) but never at the cost of clarity.
- Do NOT copy PureMac's known defects (F-0001, F-0004, F-0011, F-0012, F-0013, F-0014) and do not copy the four Pearcleaner-derived files PureMac contains (study only, see the PureMac report "Lineage").

**Disk Map side looks and feels like Radix:**
- SwiftUI `Canvas` sunburst (center radius 0.22, depth 3-10 rings, tiny children merged into "Smaller Items") and squarified treemap with bytes-proportional area, layers split into fill / label / overlay canvases, Equatable views, layout computed off the main thread and cancellable.
- Hover inspector + tooltip, double-click drill-down, breadcrumb bar, back/forward, keyboard navigation, multi-select, Quick Look, context menu (Reveal in Finder, Copy Path, Open in Terminal, Move to Trash), a staging "Discard Pile" overlay before deleting.
- Do NOT copy Radix's known defects (F-0040 sampling-based auto-summary, F-0041 double path storage per node).

**One app, one design system:** the two halves share typography, colors, spacing and materials so they read as one product; the sidebar switches between them.

entries.name: Architecture decisions
entries.content:
Durable reasons behind the v1 architecture (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, scaffold b5224eb, summary research/reports/M1-decisions.md). Read this before changing a decision; the doc says what, this says why it is hard to change.

1. **One SwiftPM target per module, not one library with folders.** Seven builders work in parallel worktrees. Separate targets make ownership a folder boundary and the dependency direction a compiler error (Cleaner cannot reach into ScanEngine internals). Package.swift declares every target up front so no builder ever needs to edit it.
2. **Concrete types, not protocols, as contracts.** Each service has one real implementation; UI snapshot mode feeds models demo *state*, not mock services, so protocols would be single-implementation abstractions. The exception worth a seam is Safety's trash backend (system vs temp-dir for tests).
3. **Core targets are not MainActor-default.** With Xcode 26 defaults a nonisolated async scan runs on the main thread (T-0011 S2). The engine owns blocking threads because the cooperative pool is only ncpu wide (S4).
4. **Placeholders are safe by construction.** The scaffold TrashService refuses everything, so three UI builders can wire real buttons without any path to real deletion. ScanEngine's placeholder is a correct but slow FileManager walk, so Cleaner and Uninstaller builders get real sizes before M2 lands.
5. **No permanent delete, no helper, no scan cache in v1.** Each is where surveyed tools shipped their worst defects (F-0012/F-0025 permanent rm; F-0002/F-0070 root helpers; F-0017/F-0037/F-0038/F-0045 caches). They can be added later behind the same door; removing a shipped mistake cannot be undone for users.
6. **Map = allocated, confirmations = frees-now.** Allocated adds up for map areas; PRIVATESIZE is the only honest promise (deleting a clone frees ~0). PRIVATESIZE costs +61-70% kernel CPU, so it is fetched per selection only.
7. **Deterministic hard-link owner (smallest path).** Parallel first-seen attribution flips per-folder sizes between identical scans (F-0054); a map whose areas move between scans looks broken.
8. **Snapshot = own-window capture through dlsym(CGWindowListCreateImage).** ImageRenderer draws NavigationSplitView/List as a yellow placeholder; cacheDisplay drops ScrollView content and glass. The window-server copy of our own off-screen window is complete and needs no Screen Recording permission (verified via `open` of the bundle, not only from Terminal). If Apple removes the symbol, the renderer falls back to cacheDisplay.
9. **Resource bundle in Contents/Resources.** SwiftPM's Bundle.module only looks beside the executable or in .build; a bundle at the .app root breaks code signing. CleanupCatalog looks in Bundle.main's Resources first.

User decisions still open: license (MIT recommended), bundle id + Developer ID enrollment, privileged helper after v1, permanent delete, default scan scope without FDA, clone dedup in the map.

entries.name: Build: Cleaner: validated cleanup catalog, in-use guard, junk scan
entries.content:
## Build: Cleaner (T-0045), branch feat/cleaner-catalog

**Key files** (all in `Sources/Cleaner/`)
- `PatternValidator.swift`: `PatternValidator.problem(with:)` and `CleanupCatalog.validated()`. Fail closed: a rule with one bad pattern is dropped whole. Runs in `CleanupCatalog.bundled()` (logs rejections via os.Logger) and again in `Cleaner.init`, so no catalog reaches expansion unvalidated.
- `Resources/catalog.json`: 27 rules. Browsers first, then developer (safe), review stores, manual items, `com.apple.*` (review), catch-all `~/Library/Caches/*`, logs (7 days). Order matters: overlaps resolve to the more specific match, and equal paths to the rule listed first (`CatalogTests.catchAllCacheRuleComesAfterEverySpecificCacheRule` guards it).
- `CatalogMatcher.swift`: in-process fnmatch expansion against realpath(home); refuses a pattern when a symlink sits above the match; drops a match that contains another match.
- `ProcessSnapshot.swift`: libproc (`proc_listpids` UID-only, `proc_pidpath`, `PROC_PIDLISTFDS` + `PROC_PIDFDVNODEPATHINFO`) → running apps (outermost .app's bundle id and CFBundleName, executable name) and open files under home. No AppKit, no fork.
- `InUseGuard.swift`: skip reasons in priority order: app named anywhere on the path below home (normalized alphanumerics, case-insensitive), open file inside, changed < 10 min (future dates count as recent), minimumAgeDays.
- `Cleaner.swift`: task group, 4 measures in flight, no time budget; vanished items dropped; measure errors become "Could not be read" with zero size; cancellation rethrown. New additive API: `CleanupItem.canClean`, `Cleaner.init(processes:)`.

**Design choices**
- No THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry: every path comes from the owning tool's own docs, not from another cleaner's rule file.
- `com.apple.*` caches are review, not safe: macOS daemons are not in `runningApplications`-style lists and some re-download data.
- A running Xcode skips DerivedData (the name match sees the `Xcode` folder). Intentional: the note says so.
- Glob only directly in `~/Library/Caches` or `~/Library/Logs`; `~/Library/Application Support/*` is refused even though it is 3 levels deep.

**Gotchas for the integrator**
- Items stream in completion order; the UI must sort.
- Item URLs are built from realpath(home), so a symlinked home yields real paths.
- `measure` placeholder: `newestModification` looks at files only; the guard depends on it covering every file.
- Tests: 30 in CleanerTests, all against `TemporaryDirectory`; one uses the real libproc snapshot with the test process holding an fd.
- Not built: phase 2 project artifacts (awaiting acceptance of phase 1).


--- 2026-09-23T12:17:46 · fix-cleaner-catalog ---
### fix-cleaner-catalog: review round 1 resolved (commit 31e540b)

**What changed**
- **Owner state (F-0015).** `CleanupRule.owners: [String]?`. A list names the apps, bundle ids or executables that use the matches. `[]` means the matches are ownerless (logs, macOS Install Data). `nil` is allowed only for the two catch-all cache rules; there the owner comes from a reverse-DNS folder name, and a folder without one is unknown. Every catalog rule now declares its owners.
- **`CleanupItem.caution`.** "Cache of an unidentified app" or "Some contents could not be read". `isPreselected` requires that it is nil, and `canClean` ignores it. The init gained `caution:` with a default, so UI callers still compile.
- **`Cleaner.recheck(_:)`.** It takes a fresh `ProcessSnapshot`, measures each item again and runs the guard again. It keeps the input order and the scan's `FileIdentity`, and it fails closed ("No longer there", "Could not be checked again"). T-0049 must call it immediately before `moveToTrash`.
- **Guard matching.** Only the declared owners and the matched name are checked, never the rule's fixed folders. A reverse-DNS name also matches when it is a sub-id of a running bundle, and its last part matches daemons (`com.apple.nsurlsessiond`). The reverse match was dropped after a read-only run on this Mac: `SafariLinkExtension` runs without Safari and would have blocked Safari's cache all day.
- **`ProcessSnapshot`.** A process gets its bundle's id and name only when it is the main executable (`X.app/Contents/MacOS/X`), so `swift` and `xcodebuild` are no longer "Xcode". A process whose fds cannot be listed while it still exists goes to `uninspected`, and the guard then fails closed. On this Mac 0 of 265 processes fail the listing.
- **`PatternValidator`.** Home patterns must lie strictly below one of the allowlisted roots: Library/{Caches,Logs,Developer,pnpm}, MobileSync/Backup, .npm, .gradle, .m2 and .cargo. The backup and installer roots are manual-only, checked in `validated()`. The old denylist code is deleted.
- **`CatalogMatcher`.** Literal leaves are matched through the directory listing with `FNM_CASEFOLD` as well, so matches carry the on-disk spelling. The symlink check is case-insensitive. The overlap check is n log n (bytewise sort, `folder/` neighbours).
- **Concurrency.** Expansion and the libproc snapshot run through `offCooperativePool` (GCD).

**Verification.** `swift build` is clean and `swift test` is 54/54 green. 15 mutations were run one at a time in a `git archive` copy, each with a targeted `--filter`, and all 15 were caught (M1-M15 on T-0045). A read-only probe on this Mac (matcher + guard, no measure, no trash) found 95 matches in 0.045 s and took the snapshot in 0.21 s. It left 8 catch-all caches unidentified and unselected, and 3 preselected.

**Open.** T-0049 must call `recheck` and show `caution`. `trashItem` should pass `allocated:` once safety-trash is merged. ScanEngine.measure cancellation is T-0043's.

### build-app-shell (T-0047), 2026-09-23

Branch `feat/app-shell`, worktree `~/projects/macontrol-wt/app-shell`. Commits: e87fd5a (probe + fake-home tests), 91e65bb (shell, Overview, onboarding, History, snapshot), 6b78faf (bundled placeholder icon). `swift build` clean with no warnings; `swift test` 33 tests in 11 suites pass.

**Key files**
- `Sources/MacontrolUI/Shell/AppModel.swift`: `scan(_ ScanScope)`, `rescan()`, `stopScan()`, `isScanning`, `scope`, `isChoosingFolder`, `volumeReadAt`, `access: AccessModel`. `fullDiskAccess` is now a computed read of `access.status`. `live()` probes once at launch and presents onboarding when the result is not `.granted`. `demo(selection:fullDiskAccess:)` gained a defaulted parameter.
- `Shell/ScanScope.swift` (Home, Macintosh HD = `/System/Volumes/Data`, folder), `ScanToolbar.swift`, `AppCommands.swift` (Cmd-1..5, Cmd-R rescan, Cmd-O Scan Folder), `SettingsView.swift`, `AppIconView.swift`, `Theme.swift` (tokens plus `card()`).
- `Onboarding/AccessModel.swift`: status, 1 s `watch()`, `appDidBecomeActive()`, `openSettings()` with legacy fallback, `suggestsRelaunch`, relaunch through `NSWorkspace.openApplication(createsNewApplicationInstance)` followed by terminate. It never shells out.
- `Overview/OverviewSummary.swift` holds the Overview's logic: capacity, largest items, safe-to-clean. The views only format.
- `History/HistoryModel.swift`: `HistoryBatch` grouping and the status wording.
- `Snapshot/SnapshotRenderer.swift`: the named `shots` list (5 screens, overview-limited, onboarding, onboarding-relaunch) and `renderIconSet`. `Sources/Macontrol/main.swift` adds `--render-icon`.

**Design choices**
- The app uses one `Window` scene rather than `WindowGroup`, because every screen shares one AppModel.
- ⌘R rescans. ARCHITECTURE section 8 had given ⌘R to Reveal in Finder, so I suggested ⇧⌘R to T-0048.
- Relaunch is offered only after the user went to Settings and came back with the probe still denied. Whether FDA reaches a running app is unverified (P5).
- The "Largest" card lists the scan root's children, files included. A folder row drills the map into that folder; a file row opens the map at the root.
- The purgeable note carries the time the volume was read (`volumeReadAt`). It is never added to available space, and it has no purge action.

**Gotchas for the integrator**
- `NSHostingView.sceneBridgingOptions = [.toolbars, .title]` makes snapshots show the toolbar and the title.
- Snapshot windows never belong to the active app. `.environment(\.controlActiveState, .key)` turns the sidebar text and the prominent buttons active. Overriding `isKeyWindow` on the NSWindow does nothing.
- Sheet-sized shots (`size: nil`) take `NSHostingView.fittingSize` and a borderless window.
- The number format follows the Mac's locale, which is why the PNGs here read "131,21 GB". Tests compare against `formattedBytes` and never against literals.
- Merge note: AppModel's init gained defaulted `access:` and `volumeReadAt:` parameters, so the other modules' initializers are unchanged.

entries.name: Build: Uninstaller: app inventory, evidence-scored leftovers, safe uninstall order
entries.content:
### build-uninstaller (T-0046), 2026-09-23

Branch `feat/uninstaller` (worktree `~/projects/macontrol-wt/uninstaller`), 3 commits on top of 3dfbfe1:
cb83df9 (inventory, leftovers, uninstall order), 86d29db (cask recall oracle, id-named Preferences folders),
then the built-in fix. `swift build` and `swift test` green: 31 tests in 10 suites, 22 of them in UninstallerTests.

**Key files (Sources/Uninstaller)**
- `Models.swift`: the public contract. Additive over the scaffold: `Leftover.launchdLabel`, `LeftoverEvidence.contentLibrary`, `UninstallPlan.bundleLaunchdLabels` and `.notes`, `UninstallError`.
- `Uninstaller.swift`: `installedApps()` (each folder plus one level of subfolders), `plan(for:)`, `uninstall(_:leftovers:)`, the blocker text and the preflight.
- `AppBundle.swift`: Info.plist read from disk (not `Bundle`, which caches per path), kind detection, the application-groups entitlement through SecStaticCode.
- `LeftoverFinder.swift`: the evidence rules. `claim(_:)` is the one identifier rule: the bundle id, or `<id>.<anything>` when the id has at least 3 parts. Another installed app with the same or a more specific id gives the item a note ("Also used by X").
- `LaunchdJob.swift` (plist parsing), `LaunchdControl.swift` (the only `Process` in the app, `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label>`, exit 3 = not loaded, accepted).
- `UninstallActions.swift`: the injectable side effects (quit, bootout, moveToTrash), and `RunningApps.quit` (terminate, poll `isTerminated` for up to 10 s on the main actor).
- `FileSystem.swift`: small read-only helpers and `offCooperativePool`, which runs blocking I/O on GCD rather than the cooperative pool.

**Design choices**
- Sub-identifiers (`<id>.ShipIt`, `<id>.ShareExtension`) are preselected, unless another installed app claims them. Reading embedded bundle ids added nothing, because appex ids have to be prefixed by the app id anyway.
- Containers: metadata (`MCMMetadataIdentifier`) wins over the folder name. It is read only for UUID-named folders and folders named like the app, not for all ~300 containers.
- App groups: other apps' entitlements are read only when the app declares groups (about 0.2 s warm for 73 apps). Built-in apps are skipped there, and built-in apps get no leftovers at all.
- `/Library` items are always `needsAdministrator`. Items in home that this user cannot move are too.
- Receipts and in-bundle LaunchDaemons become `plan.notes`. v1 cannot act on them.
- A root-owned bundle (Xcode, most App Store apps) gets a blocker, but its leftovers are still listed.

**Gotchas for the integrator**
- `plan()` latency is mostly `engine.measure(app.url)`: Xcode took 15 s on the placeholder engine, Maccy 0.4 s.
- The placeholder `TrashService` refuses everything, so a live uninstall does nothing until T-0044 lands. Tests never reach it (`UninstallActions` is injected).
- The preflight calls `ProtectedPaths.refusal(for:home:)`, so T-0044 must keep that signature (commented there).
- `Tests/UninstallerTests/CaskOracle.swift` is test-only BSD-2 data with the licence inline. It is not in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, which I do not own.
- AppGroupTests ad-hoc signs a copy of /usr/bin/true with `codesign` (a Process in a test, local only, about 50 ms).
- F-0072 stays open: BTM records are not decoded.
- No UI or PNG attachments from this task: I own no UI paths. The contract notes for the screens are on T-0049.


--- 2026-09-23T12:17:16 · fix-uninstaller ---
### fix-uninstaller: review round 1 (c6677c2 on feat/uninstaller)
Changes:
- LeftoverFinder.groupContainers: only plain group names count (not "", ".", "..", no "/" or NUL). A Group Containers folder is accepted only when its containermanagerd metadata names the group; Application Scripts/<group> relies on the name check. Built-in apps are now in the rival map (group.com.apple.notes stays with Notes).
- LeftoverFinder.launchdJobs: otherUser(of:) adds "Also used by X" (X is listed in AssociatedBundleIdentifiers) or "Starts X" (X's bundle holds the program) on every launchd candidate, including in-bundle and associated ones.
- mainIdentifier: only reverse-DNS ids with at least 2 parts are evidence. A one-word id (PyInstaller) leaves only unselected exact-name items.
- Uninstaller.uninstall: a backstop refuses any leftover not 2+ levels inside home/Library or root/Library (standardized path, no NUL), before any step. The running check repeats after the last bootout. checkUnchanged treats a nil identity as changed.
- RunningApps.isInstance: matches this bundle and its helpers, plus a same-id process running from /AppTranslocation/. It no longer quits a separate copy of the app.
- Test Recorder: quitResults gives each quit call its own answer.
Tests added: malformedAppGroupNeverNamesAFolderOutsideItsOwnContainer, groupContainerNeedsItsOwnMetadata, groupSharedWithABuiltInAppIsNotPreselected, agentAssociatedWithAnotherInstalledAppIsNotedAndUnselected, singleWordIdentifierIsNotEvidence, appRelaunchedBeforeItsJobsStoppedStopsBeforeTrashing, leftoverOutsideALibraryFolderIsRefusedBeforeAnyStep, itemWithoutARecordedIdentityCountsAsChanged, onlyThisBundleAndItsHelpersCountAsRunning. The order test now pins quit, bootouts, quit, trash. The package has 40 tests, all green.
Proof: two mutation passes (scratchpad/fix-uninstaller/mutate.py A|B). Each pass reverted 4-5 fixes, and exactly the matching tests failed.
Real Mac, read-only: 111 of 111 group containers have MCMMetadataIdentifier == folder name. Application Scripts group folders have no metadata. Reading entitlements for 94 apps takes 0.3-0.9 s, of which /System apps take 0.2-0.3 s.
Open: #8 (rival ids via Launch Services, which needs an injected lookup), #9 (vendor subfolder names, left to the UI), F-0072 (BTM). The ARCHITECTURE section 7 order text went to the architect as a comment on T-0046.


--- 2026-09-23T12:42:02 · fix-uninstaller ---
### fix-uninstaller, review round 2 (T-0046), 2026-09-23
Commits b64a18a and afb0996 on feat/uninstaller. 49 package tests green, 40 of them in UninstallerTests.
- **Uninstall order:** the bundle is trashed alone. Leftovers go in a second batch only if the bundle comes back `.trashed` and its path is empty afterwards. Otherwise each leftover is reported `.failed("Not moved, because <App> is still installed.")`. The report carries the bundle's batch id, and History shows two batches.
- **Identity:** `itemToTrash(for:)` passes the current identity for a leftover that is still a regular file, both at the pre-quit check and after the final quit. The reason is that cfprefsd rewrites preference plists when the app quits. The bundle, folders and links stay strict.
- **UninstallError** conforms to LocalizedError, one sentence per case.
- **plan(for:)** checks for cancellation after the inventory, before each measure, and before the bundle measure.
- **App groups:** only `group.` or `<teamID>.` names count (`AppBundle.teamIdentifier`, `LeftoverFinder.isAppGroup`).
- **Bundle launchd labels:** a label counts only when the job runs the bundle's own program (BundleProgram relative without `..`, or Program / ProgramArguments[0] inside the bundle). Launchd paths with `..` never count as inside.
- **blocker:** reports "Locked in Finder" for UF_IMMUTABLE before the "owned by the system" check.
- **Test recorder:** it now really moves items into `<fixture>/Trash` (refusing anything outside the fixture), and has `whileQuitting`, `refusedPath` and `afterTrashing` hooks.
- **Not done:** TrashItem.allocated. The scaffold TrashItem lacks it, so the integrator adds 2 arguments at the merge (see the T-0046 comment).
- **Verification:** mutation passes A/B/C (scratchpad/fix-uninstaller/r2/mutate.py). The reviewer's 6 probes pass against the real Safety overlay (scratchpad/fix-uninstaller/r2/overlay). F-0030 is set to fixed.

entries.name: Build: Safety: protected-path policy, Move to Trash with identity checks, undo journal
entries.content:
## Build: Safety (T-0044), branch feat/safety-trash, commits b4e27f7, 6e52add, 6fbe2cf

**Key files (Sources/Safety):**
- `ProtectedPaths.swift`: `ProtectedPaths.refusal(for:home:cloudConfirmed:)` (public), `canonicalPath(of:)` (F_GETPATH on the parent + leaf as written; `.`/`..` leaves resolve the whole path), `ProtectionPolicy` (rules built once per home/batch).
- `ProtectedLocations.swift`: data only. Roots from Homebrew SYSTEM_DIRS/UNDELETABLE_PATHS, never-touch areas, PureMac provider state, cloud folders, license texts at the end.
- `TrashService.swift`: public types, `TrashBackend` (`.finder` = FileManager.trashItem), the actor (runs on its own DispatchSerialQueue executor, off the cooperative pool).
- `TrashBatch.swift`: per-call order: drop descendants of already-trashed items, policy, identity, keep expansion, trash, journal.
- `TrashJournal.swift`: `JournalEntry` + JSON Lines reader/writer.

**Design choices:**
- Order of checks in the policy: location (string, lowercased, containment) -> lstat item + parent -> different st_dev (mount point / firmlink root) -> flags -> read-only volume / com.apple.rootless -> cloud -> can rename (parent W_OK, dir itself W_OK, sticky parent ownership).
- `sunlnk` (SF_NOUNLINK) is on /Applications, /Library, /Users, /usr/local: it blocks only the item itself, so it is checked on the item, never on the parent.
- Other users' homes and /Users/Shared are refused (`/Users/<x>`), `~/.Trash` and any `.Trashes` component are never-touch.
- Journal: append-only; restore = a second line with restored=true, merged by (batch, trashedPath) in `entries()`. Opened O_RDWR|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW 0600 so a torn tail can be read and closed with a newline. A failed journal write stops the rest of the batch (`.failed`), a journal that cannot be opened refuses the whole batch.
- Undo uses `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` after an identity check of the trashed item: "only if the original path is free" is atomic.
- `expectedIdentity == nil` is allowed (identity is recorded, not compared).

**Gotchas for the integrator:**
- `rm` is aliased to `rm -i` in this shell profile: a scripted `rm file` blocks forever waiting for 'y'. Use `command rm -f`.
- Folder URLs from FileManager/appendingPathComponent may carry a trailing slash, so `TrashOutcome` URLs compare unequal to a scan's URL. Compare `.path`.
- `RefusalReason.notImplemented` is gone; `RefusalReason` is now `Error` (typed throws).
- THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md needs the Homebrew + PureMac entries (asked on T-0003).
- UninstallerTests builds `TrashService(journalURL:)` with the real Finder backend. It only calls `plan` today; any test that calls `uninstall` must pass `backend:` (asked on T-0046).
- Not done (ponytail): per-item progress/cancellation for huge batches; sizes of folders pieced out by `keep` are 0 in the journal; iCloud "Desktop & Documents" sync is not detected (Radix does not either); live `/private/var/folders/*/*/{T,C}` of running apps is left to the cleaner's in-use guard.


--- 2026-09-23T12:31:46 · fix-safety-trash ---
### fix-safety-trash: review round 1 fixes (feat/safety-trash @ 31fc928)
- **TrashBatch keep now fails closed.** Keep URLs are resolved with `try? map` instead of `compactMap`: if one throws, the whole item is `.failed` and nothing moves. Keep paths, child paths and the `trashed` keys are all lowercased. A keep equal to the item moves nothing.
- **Every item gets an outcome.** When no piece moved and no outcome names the item, it gets `.failed(item.url, "Nothing in it was moved…")`. A child that vanished after listing reports `.refused(child, .missing)`. `trashedAncestor` checks the path itself before its ancestors, so duplicates and selections inside a split item report `.trashed`.
- **ProtectionPolicy refuses a folder that contains a mount.** It checks `getfsstat(MNT_NOWAIT)` `f_mntonname` for the prefix `canonical + "/"`, lowercased. If the mount table cannot be read, it refuses. The kernel lists mount names in F_GETPATH form (checked with /tmp and /System/Volumes/Data spellings).
- `ProtectedPaths.unreachable(errno)`: EACCES, EPERM and ENAMETOOLONG map to `.needsAdministrator`, anything else to `.missing`. It is used in canonicalPath and both lstat calls.
- The default-home policy is a static and built once. 2000 calls take 0.40 s, down from 2.69 s.
- The sink audit gained a whole-word regex for removefile, copyfile, posix_spawn(p), popen, exec*, system. It skips `.system(size:)`.
- `RefusalReason.notImplemented` is restored for the UI branches' switches.
- New tests: keepSurvivesWhenItsFolderCannotBeOpened, keepSurvivesWhenTheItemIsSpelledInAnotherCase, anItemWithNothingLeftToMoveReportsItself, aDuplicateSelectionIsReportedAsTrashed, aDeepItemIsNotReportedMissing, refusesAFolderThatContainsAMountPoint (MACONTROL_DISK_IMAGE_TESTS=1), cCallsAreFoundAsWholeWords. Mutations N1-N6 each turned the suite red (T-0044 comment).


--- 2026-09-23T12:54:48 · fix-safety-trash ---
### Fix round 2 (fix-safety-trash, review-safety-trash-2), commit 8fee903

What changed, per review issue:

- **Cloud provider folders are roots (high).** Every folder directly inside `~/Library/Mobile Documents` and `~/Library/CloudStorage` (iCloud Drive's `com~apple~CloudDocs`, each app container, each CloudStorage domain) is refused even with `cloudConfirmed`. What is inside still passes after confirmation.
- **keep is one set per batch (F-0026).** `TrashBatch.process(_:)` resolves the keep of every item once, fails the whole batch closed if one keep cannot be resolved, and applies the set to every item before the trashed-ancestor shortcut. An item at or inside a kept path is not moved.
- **Volume system folders.** `.Spotlight-V100`, `.fseventsd` and `.DocumentRevisions-V100` moved to `neverTouchNames`, so they are refused on every volume.
- **Journal folder.** `ProtectionPolicy(home:journal:)` makes the journal's folder never-touch, and the folders holding it roots. `TrashService` now builds the policy per batch, after opening the journal, so a folder created on first use still resolves to its canonical path. The UI pre-check protects the default journal folder too.
- **On-disk leaf name.** `canonicalPath` appends the leaf's stored name, from `getattrlistat(ATTR_CMN_NAME, FSOPT_NOFOLLOW)` on the parent fd. Undo therefore puts `report.pdf` back as `report.pdf`.
- **Case-sensitive twins.** `trashedAncestor` accepts a case-insensitive key match only when the item has left its path and something exists at the computed Trash location.
- **Undo does not follow links.** `renamex_np` gets `RENAME_EXCL | RENAME_NOFOLLOW_ANY`, and `ELOOP` has its own message. A trashed symlink leaf still restores.
- **Sink audit.** Any whole-word use of `Process` outside Uninstaller/Launchd*, plus `OSAScript`, `NSUserAppleScriptTask` and `SBApplication`, pinned with positive and negative samples. None of the branches has a hit.

Tests: 9 new ones (see the T-0044 comments). `TrashFixture.attachDiskImage(_:at:)` replaces the private hdiutil helper and detaches in deinit. swift test is 48/48. The env-gated disk-image tests pass when run alone. In one batched mutation run, the 9 new tests failed and the old ones did not.

Open: whether FileProvider itself would block a rename of a provider root is still unverified (no iCloud account here). Keep is still compared lowercased on case-sensitive volumes, which can keep more than asked, never less.

entries.name: Build: Disk map: sunburst and treemap, drill-down, inspector, staging tray
entries.content:
### Build: Disk map (T-0048), branch feat/disk-map, worktree ~/projects/macontrol-wt/disk-map

Commits: d1d890d geometry + palette, c000c68 model + pile + trash splice, ecd44da screen, 0fbb41e F-0040 test hardening.
`swift build` and `swift test` green (35 tests, 10 suites; 26 of them are the disk map's).

**Key files** (all in `Sources/MacontrolUI/DiskMap/`)
- `MapLayout.swift`: `MapStyle`, `MapItem` (`.node` / `.smallerItems(parent, members)`), `MapElement`, `LayoutKey` (cache key: treeVersion, focus, style, whole-point size, scale), `MapLayout` (elements in BFS order, each parent's children contiguous, `element(at:)` hit test that descends the hierarchy). Also `ScanTree.sortedChildren/isExpandable/path(to:)` (nonisolated, iterative).
- `MapLayoutBuilder.swift`: sunburst (hole 0.22, ≤ 6 rings, ring count shrinks to the depth actually drawn) and squarified treemap (Bruls et al., own implementation, 16 pt headers, 2 pt inset, containers ≥ 48×40 pt). `@concurrent layout(of:for:)` runs off the main actor; `Task.checkCancellation()` per queue item.
- `MapPalette.swift`: 8 branch hues + grey, fade toward the background by depth (0.1 per level, max 0.5).
- `DiskMapModel.swift` (+`+Trash`): scan states, navigation history, selection, side-list rows, layout cache (12 entries), review flow, `apply(_ report:)` splice.
- `DiscardPile.swift`: add-time refusals (scan root, `.removed`, `.systemProtected`, `.mountPoint`, `ProtectedPaths`, already staged, inside a staged folder); staging a folder absorbs staged items inside it.
- Views: `DiskMapScreen` (empty / scanning / workspace, keyboard), `MapChart` (layout task, hover, clicks, tooltip, VoiceOver children), `MapCanvas` (fill layer Equatable on the layout key; highlight layer for hover/selection/staged hatch), `MapHeader`, `InspectorPanel`, `ItemList`, `DiscardPileBar`, `ReviewSheet`, `DiskMapActions` (Reveal, Quick Look, Copy Path, Open in Terminal; no file mutation).
- `DemoTree.swift`: ~1,100-node seeded home folder with packages, an unreadable folder, iCloud dataless files and a hard link; the demo model stages DerivedData and an Xcode .xip and selects Library.

**Design choices**
- No Radix code copied: the geometry is written from the published squarify algorithm; only the 0.22 hole ratio and the overall look follow Radix. So no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry was needed.
- Merge rule: children sorted by size; the first child whose wedge arc (at the ring's outer edge, assuming 6 rings) is under 4 device px, or whose tile is under 100 px², and everything smaller, become one "smaller items" element holding every member. Decided on every child, never a sample (F-0040). Folder own bytes: an undrawn gap in both charts, a "Folder entries" row in the list.
- Colour by top-level branch (slot = position among the focus's drawn children); `MapPalette.slot` avoids the ring closing on two neighbours of one colour.
- The layout on screen stays until the next one is ready (stretched to the new size), so resizes and drills never blank the map. Drill/style changes cross-fade with a scale (opacity only under Reduce Motion).
- Keyboard: chart area is focusable; Return open, Esc and ⌘↑ up, arrows previous/next sibling, Space Quick Look; ⌘[ ⌘] ⌘↑ ⌘R ⌘⌫ are button shortcuts (⌘⌫ only when a real selection exists, never stages the folder being viewed).
- Trash: `confirmReview` → `TrashService.moveToTrash` (or all `.notImplemented` refusals when no service) → `apply` splices `.trashed` items with `removeSubtree`, bumps `treeVersion`, drops cached layouts, moves focus/history/selection off removed nodes; refusals stay in the pile with the reason as a note.

**Gotchas for the integrator**
- Swift Testing runs a `@MainActor` test body inside a main-queue job, so `SnapshotRenderer`'s `RunLoop.main.run` cannot run other main-actor jobs: `.task` work never completes during a test render (the map shows its spinner in `SnapshotTests`). `Macontrol --snapshot` is fine. `DiskMapSnapshotTests` precomputes the layout first.
- `DiskMapText.refusal` is an exhaustive switch over `RefusalReason`: a new case from T-0044 breaks the build there on purpose.
- Outcomes are matched to staged items by `original.standardizedFileURL.path`; T-0044 must echo the URL it was given.
- F-0063 residual belongs to T-0043: removing the charged link while another link survives subtracts bytes still on disk.
- `focus` is still publicly settable (Overview uses it); a direct set does not add a Back entry.
- Shots: `MACONTROL_SHOTS=<dir> swift test --filter DiskMapSnapshotTests` writes sunburst/treemap light/dark and the review sheet (confirm, refused).

**Numbers**: 1,010,101-node tree, focus root, 1000×700 pt @2x, debug: sunburst 20-24 ms (200 elements), treemap 37-49 ms (10,100 elements). Palette closest pair dE00: normal 15.72, deutan 14.96, protan 15.21.


--- 2026-09-23T12:30:07 · fix-disk-map ---
### fix-disk-map: review round 1 (feat/disk-map @ 9d9a156)
**Changed**
- MapChart: hover is `MapHover(key:index:)` and resolves only against the layout it came from, so a stale index can no longer trap in `.contextMenu`, whose closure runs on every body evaluation.
- DiskMapModel+Trash: `confirmReview` applies the report before touching `review`. Cancel and interactive dismiss are off while moving. `ReviewState` gained `cloudConfirmed`, `cloudItemCount`, `canConfirm` and `isIncomplete`.

entries.name: Build: Scan engine: fd-relative parallel getattrlistbulk walker, exact sizes, frees-now estimate
entries.content:
## Build: scan engine (T-0043), branch feat/scan-engine, 3 commits on 3dfbfe1

**Key files**
- `Sources/ScanEngine/FolderWalk.swift`: the parallel walk. Blocking `Thread` pool, one LIFO job stack and a `pending` counter under one `NSCondition`. Folder records are index-based (no class chains, so no recursive deinit at depth). Parent fds are ref-counted; over the descriptor budget the shallowest idle parent is closed and later reopened by name from an open ancestor with a (dev, ino) check. EMFILE/ENFILE from outside: retry 5 s, then `.incomplete`.
- `Sources/ScanEngine/BulkReader.swift`: `getattrlistbulk` into a 256 KiB heap buffer per worker. The record layout was verified with a C probe: with PACK_INVAL, ERROR comes right after the returned set, dir attrs are packed only for VDIR, file attrs only for non-dirs, and ext attrs for every entry.
- `TreeSink.swift` (tree plus the "/" to Data-volume placement), `MeasureSink.swift`, `ReclaimSink.swift` + `Selection.swift` (frees-now). They are called only under the walk lock.
- `Sources/MacontrolCore/ScanTree.swift`: name byte arena, 52 B/node. `finalizeTotals()` charges each hard link group to its smallest path.
- `Sources/mcscan/main.swift`: `-A`, `-j N`, `--stats`. Its `research/bench/run.sh` TOOLS line is `mcscan`.

**Numbers.** Fixture total 2,368,040,960 B, identical per-folder sizes in 20/20 runs. Apparent size matches ground truth. run.sh at load 9.6: 1.259 s against dua's 1.045 s (1.20x). At load 4: 0.69 s against 0.68 s. Tree: 75.8 B/node with names and slack. Max RSS: 56 MB.

**Design choices the integrator should know**
- Workers are 1.5 per active core, capped at 12, not the architecture's 8. The walk is I/O-latency bound past kern.maxvnodes. The sweep is on T-0043.
- The first open of a folder is not identity-checked, because the listing just named it. Roots and reopens are checked. Safety re-checks identity before any delete anyway.
- Clone dedup is not implemented in the map (spike: CLONEID alone costs < 10% kernel CPU). The decision is the architect's; see the T-0043 comment.
- `reclaimable()` lists each selected file's parent once and matches entries by name (String equality, so NFC and NFD match). Two links of one inode are two items; a firmlink alias of one item is the same item.
- No third-party code was copied. The ideas behind the attribute set, the pool and termination come from OpenDisk/dua reports, so there is no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry.

**Gotchas**
- `UTType(filenameExtension:)` defaults to conforming to public.data, so `.app` is never a package. Pass `conformingTo: .directory`.
- Building a 4,000-level chain in place takes 75 s of kernel time: each mkdir costs time in proportion to its depth. Tests build it in 100-level segments and move them into place with renameat (10 s total). A scan at that depth costs about 3 s of kernel time for the same reason.
- `rm` on this machine is interactive (alias). Use `unlink` for a symlink you created.
- `research/bench/fixtures/` in .gitignore does not match a symlink. Remove any fixture symlink before you commit.


--- 2026-09-23T12:35:33 · fix-scan-engine ---
### fix-scan-engine: review round 1 fixes (commit 4131bda)
- **ReclaimSink**: BulkEntry keeps the raw EXT_FLAGS (`extendedFlags`, with `mayShareBlocks` and `sharesAllBlocks`). A compressed file with EF_SHARES_ALL_BLOCKS goes to sharedElsewhere. C probe: a compressed clone pair reports 0x41; after the clone is deleted, 0x1. A MAY_SHARE rule would have under-promised every compressed file that was ever cloned.
- **ScanTree.removeSubtree**: `rechargeHardLinks(ownedUnder:)` does a DFS of the removed subtree for owner links, then one pass over the nodes. The smallest surviving path takes the charge, and its ancestors get the bytes back (F-0063).
- **FolderWalk**: `openWaiting` is the single EMFILE/ENFILE wait (spill our own idle descriptors, else wait, up to 5 s). The first open and every reopen step use it. `reopen` pins its anchor while the lock is released, and `pinDescriptor` handles a concurrent reopen of the same folder. `ScanOptions`: the soft limit is raised once to min(hard, OPEN_MAX), and the budget is soft/4, at most 1024.
- **Startup disk**: `DataVolumeLayout.forStartupDisk` accepts "/" and /System/Volumes/Data. The tree root is "/".
- **Selection.readFiles**: a selected name missing from the listing marks the estimate incomplete.
- `stopDatalessMaterialization()` now runs on the scan, measure/reclaimable and walker threads.
- **Tests**: cloneOfACompressedFileFreesNothing, removingTheChargedLinkMovesItsBytesToTheNextLink, dataVolumeAndSlashAreBothTheStartupDisk, selectionSpelledInAnotherCaseIsALowerBound, and DescriptorPressureTests (env MACONTROL_FD_PRESSURE=1). All were mutation-checked in a scratch copy. 42 tests green, and BenchFixtureTests 20/20 exact.
- **Not done**: issue 7 (Data-side partial prefixes such as /System and /usr stay at user-facing paths; they are .systemProtected); issue 9 (a cancelled measure on a hung mount, Listing capacity); the worker-policy sign-off.


--- 2026-09-23T12:52:23 · fix-scan-engine ---
### Fix round 2 (fix-scan-engine), commit 5500175

- HIGH: `ItemMeasurement.newestModification` is now max(mtime, ctime) over every entry, folders included, plus the item's own lstat times (file branch: max(st_mtime, st_ctime)). mtime is a claim tools make (curl --remote-time, tar, unzip); ctime is the kernel's record and cannot be backdated. Renames/deletes inside a folder only move that folder's times, hence folders count. The engine never returns nil for it any more.
- `BulkReader(extended: Bool)` became `BulkReader(_ extras: Extras)` with `.changeTime` and `.reclaim`. Each `WalkSink` declares `static var extras`, so the walk requests exactly what the sink reads (TreeSink [], MeasureSink .changeTime, ReclaimSink .reclaim) and the `extended:` parameter is gone from `ScanEngine.walk` and `FolderWalk.init`. Disk-map scan cost unchanged.
- LOW: `ScanTree.removeSubtree` guards with `isInTree` (no double subtraction or UInt64 trap for a node inside a removed folder).
- LOW: `Selection` resolves ancestors with stat, so `link/f.bin` beside the selected folder `link` points to is counted once.
- LOW (doc): ScanOptions.workerCount doc points at resolvedWorkerCount. Worker policy and '/' layout still wait on the architect.
- Tests: new MeasureRecencyTests (5), ScanTreeTests +1, ReclaimTests +1; 49 total green. Mutation-checked in a scratch copy, 2 builds, 7 mutations, each caught.

entries.name: Build: Clean and Uninstall screens
entries.content:
## Build: Clean and Uninstall screens (T-0049, feat/clean-uninstall-ui)

**Branch:** feat/clean-uninstall-ui in ~/projects/macontrol-wt/clean-uninstall-ui, 6 commits on 3dfbfe1. swift build clean, swift test 38/38.

### Key files
- `Sources/MacontrolUI/Clean/CleanModel.swift`: streaming scan, checked set (only cleanable items), `refreshEstimate()` (ScanEngine.reclaimable, cancelled by `.task(id: selection)`, 200 ms debounce), `SpaceEstimate` (working / freesNow / atMost), `CleanReview` (fixed item list, nestedCount, hiddenBySearch), `apply(report)` → In Trash.
- `Clean/CleanScreen.swift`, `CleanRow.swift` (row + SafetyBadge popover), `CleanReviewSheet.swift`, `CleanModel+Demo.swift` (every state: safe, review, manual, skipped x2, unreadable inside).
- `Clean/TrashSheet.swift`: generic confirmation, run and outcomes sheet shared by Clean and Uninstall; `FileIcon`; `[URL].removingNested()`.
- `Clean/TrashOutcome+Words.swift`: plain words for every outcome and RefusalReason, `TrashReport.trashedURLs/summary`.
- `Clean/SearchField.swift`: Cmd-F via a hidden button (`searchable` has no focus API before macOS 15).
- `Clean/CleanDisplay.swift`: category/safety titles, colours, icons; `CleanupItem.isCleanable`; `URL.displayPath/revealInFinder()`.
- `Uninstall/UninstallModel.swift`: sections, search, lazy sizes (`measureIfNeeded` from row `.task`), plan cache, running check (NSRunningApplication), leftover choice (admin never), `UninstallConfirmation`, `apply(report,to:)`.
- `Uninstall/UninstallScreen.swift` (HSplitView list + `UninstallSheet`), `AppDetailView.swift`, `UninstallDisplay.swift`, `UninstallModel+Demo.swift` (running third-party app with every evidence kind, a shared leftover and an admin-only one; GarageBand with an admin library; Chess, Safari and Photo Booth as part of macOS). `demo(showing:)` picks the open app.

### Design choices
- Highlight (List selection) and checked state are separate. Only Space turns highlight into checks, and only the checked set feeds a batch (F-0050).
- Two guards on every batch: setters refuse manual, skipped and admin-only items, and the batch builders filter again. Mutation tests prove both.
- The review sheet fixes its item list when it opens. The same array is sent to TrashService. Clean drops nested items first and says how many.
- "Frees about X now" is ScanEngine.reclaimable. When that fails the footer says "frees at most <allocated>", never a bare allocated figure (F-0004). Trashed bytes are shown as "In Trash" (F-0042).
- The Uninstall button is hidden whenever `plan.blocker != nil` (any kind), and `builtIn` shows the lock notice and no leftovers.
- Tests never move anything: batches use nonexistent paths in their own TemporaryDirectory plus bogus identities, so the real `.finder` backend refuses them too.

### Gotchas for the integrator
- Merging feat/uninstaller: `LeftoverEvidence.contentLibrary` breaks the exhaustive switches in UninstallDisplay (on purpose). Add its title, explanation and symbol and put it in displayOrder (suggested text is on T-0046). Show `UninstallPlan.notes` as Notices. UninstallError needs LocalizedError, or the sheet shows "The operation couldn't be completed".
- Merging feat/cleaner-catalog: `CleanupItem.canClean` equals the UI's `isCleanable`. Either works.
- `CleanModel`/`UninstallModel` gained `engine: ScanEngine? = ScanEngine()`. AppModel.live() may pass the shared engine.
- Snapshot PNGs render the window inactive, so prominent buttons and checkboxes are grey. A presented sheet dims its parent window, so set `model.review = nil` before rendering the screen.
- `#require(array.first(where: \.keyPath))` does not compile (rethrows plus key path inside the macro). Use a trailing closure.
- Set `MACONTROL_SNAPSHOT_DIR=<dir> swift test --filter "CleanSnapshotTests|UninstallSnapshotTests"` to write the 16 PNGs.


--- 2026-09-23T13:05:33 · fix-clean-uninstall-ui ---
### fix-clean-uninstall-ui (T-0049 fix round 1), 2026-09-23, commit ec8d76a

- Merged feat/cleaner-catalog (31e540b, accepted) and feat/uninstaller (afb0996) into feat/clean-uninstall-ui. Each branch touches only its own files, so there were no conflicts. The duplicate `CleanupItem.isCleanable` extension was removed in favour of the real `canClean`.
- Clean: confirmReview runs `cleaner.recheck` right before the trash. Only canClean items move. Rechecked items are written back into the list, and held items show "Not moved: <reason>" in the sheet (the new `notMoved` on TrashSheet). An empty batch is never sent. scan() runs the stream in a task the model owns, so navigation no longer cancels it. `estimateKey` stays nil during a scan, so no estimate walk runs until the scan ends. Rows show `caution`. The headline shows cleanableBytes. hiddenBySearch counts listed rows. A change of query clears the highlight.
- Uninstall: loadPlan plans again on each selection, showing the last plan meanwhile, with a 150 ms debounce. loadApps runs on every visit, drops plans and sizes whose identity changed, and has an error state. rescan() is behind Scan Again (detail header and plan error) and runs automatically after any failed uninstall. Choices live in `choices[app][leftover]` and are seeded once per leftover. beginUninstall rereads the running state. The confirmation lists launchd bootouts and plan notes (F-0069). contentLibrary got its section. Bundle sizes are measured 3 at a time, and icons are cached per path.
- Tests: 9 new or rewritten (Clean 5, Uninstall 6 incl. rewrite of uninstallSendsExactlyTheListedItems onto RecordedActions). The whole package passes 132/132. In mutation passes A and B, all 11 reverted fixes were caught.
- Open: ReclaimEstimate.isIncomplete (needs feat/scan-engine); plan() measures the bundle a second time (needs a T-0046 API); no leftovers-only view after a partial uninstall; the snapshot-only band above sheet headers.


--- 2026-09-23T13:24:43 · fix-clean-uninstall-ui ---
### Review round 2 fixes (fix-clean-uninstall-ui, be77974)

- **Leftover choices (high).** `UninstallModel.choices` stores only the user's own checks as `LeftoverChoice(chosen, note, wasPreselected)`. `isChosen` = user choice ?? current plan's `isPreselected`. `show()` drops a user's check when the leftover gains a note or loses preselection. There is no seeding any more, so a re-plan that adds "Also used by X" unchecks the item. `leftoverSelection` is now get-only.
- **Blocked apps.** Reveal in Finder on the blocker notice (not for built-in apps) and in the app row's context menu. No Apple notice next to a blocker. `isChosen`/`setChosen` are off while `canUninstall` is false, and the checkboxes are disabled. `canUninstall` also requires `plan.app.id == selectedApp`. Demo: root-owned Pages plan (`DemoApps.pages`).
- **Search.** `query.didSet` clears `selectedApp` when the search hides it.
- **TrashSheet.** Notes are a List section ("Also happens", then "Moves to the Trash"). Outcome rows that did not move get Reveal in Finder.
- **Uninstall errors.** `UninstallConfirmation.failureMessage(for:)`. After stillRunning/bootoutFailed it says the app was asked to quit and which background items may have been stopped.
- **Clean.** `scan()` resets the estimate, In Trash rows are replaced by URL, and `inScreenOrder` is shared by the groups and the review. `confirmReview` uses the Trash only when a cleaner exists (fails closed).
- **Open:** measureIfNeeded requeue race (low), and a leftovers-only entry after a partial uninstall (low).
- **Tests:** aLeftoverThatGainsANoteIsNoLongerChosen(x2), aBlockedAppHasNoUninstallAndNoChosenLeftovers, searchingAwayFromTheSelectedAppDeselectsIt, aLateStopSaysWhatAlreadyRan, outcomesApplyToTheNewestPlan, withoutACleanerNothingReachesTheTrash, reviewRowsFollowTheScreenOrder, aCacheTrashedTwiceIsOneInTrashRow, scanningAgainResetsTheEstimate, manyNotesLeaveTheItemListItsRoom, blockedAppRenders. Mutation-checked: the note-drop and the sheet layout tests fail on the old code.

app-shell 6b78faf, disk-map 9d9a156, clean-uninstall-ui be77974 (it already contained cleaner-catalog and uninstaller).
